title: Set-Returning Functions & TABLE Output
description: Build table functions using RETURNS TABLE and generate series using generate_series().

data.text: A **Set-Returning Function (SRF)** returns a set of rows (a virtual table) rather than a single scalar value. SRFs can be called directly inside the `FROM` clause of queries.

data.title: Custom Set-Returning Table Function
data.content: Returning tabular records using RETURNS TABLE and RETURN QUERY.
data.code:
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION get_active_subscribers_by_domain(p_domain TEXT)
RETURNS TABLE (
    subscriber_id INT,
    email VARCHAR,
    subscribed_at TIMESTAMPTZ
) AS $$
BEGIN
    RETURN QUERY
    SELECT id, s.email, s.created_at
    FROM subscribers s
    WHERE s.email LIKE '%@' || p_domain
      AND s.is_active = true;
END;
$$ LANGUAGE plpgsql STABLE;

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Set-returning functions return tables via `RETURNS TABLE (...)`.
Use `RETURN QUERY` to stream rows directly from internal queries.
Call set-returning functions in the `FROM` clause like ordinary tables.
